title: Clarity of Scripture
definition: The Clarity of Scripture means God has spoken in a way that His people can truly understand what is necessary for salvation, faith, and obedience.
summary: The Clarity of Scripture means God has spoken in a way that His people can truly understand what is necessary for salvation, faith, and obedience.
christFocus: Jesus taught the Scriptures plainly, opened the understanding of His disciples, and still calls ordinary people to hear, receive, and obey God’s Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture is clear enough to lead people to Christ and guide them in faithful living. Some passages are difficult and require careful study, humility, and patience, but God has not hidden the way of salvation from ordinary believers.

The clarity of Scripture does not mean every believer will understand everything immediately. It means God’s Word can be read, taught, translated, explained, and obeyed. Children, new believers, people in hardship, and those without formal training can truly receive the truth God has made known.

Jesus expected people to read and understand Scripture. He corrected misunderstanding, opened hearts, and taught with authority. The clarity of Scripture honors both God’s kindness in speaking and the Holy Spirit’s work in helping believers understand.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel disqualified from studying the Bible because they think Scripture belongs only to scholars, pastors, or people who grew up in church. The clarity of Scripture gives courage to the ordinary believer who wants to know God but feels intimidated.

This doctrine also protects people from dependence on controlling teachers who act as if God’s Word can only be understood through them. Christ gives His people pastors and teachers, but He does not hide His Word from His sheep.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to Scripture humbly and expectantly. Use good teaching, ask questions, study carefully, and pray for the Holy Spirit’s help, but do not believe the lie that God’s Word is closed to you. Read with the aim of knowing Christ and obeying what He makes clear.
